pageCache.text:
Personal, Social, Health, Economic and Citizenship Education
At Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy, we believe that PSHCE plays a vital role in helping children become happy, healthy, confident and respectful members of society. Through our PSHCE curriculum, children develop the knowledge, skills and values they need to build positive relationships, look after their physical and mental wellbeing, stay safe and prepare for life beyond primary school.
We teach PSHCE using the Jigsaw programme, a comprehensive scheme of learning that fully supports the statutory requirements for Relationships Education, Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) and Health Education. We have chosen to invest in this high quality programme to ensure our curriculum remains up to date and reflects current guidance and best practice.
The Jigsaw curriculum is organised into six half-termly themes:
Being Me in My World Celebrating Difference Dreams and Goals Healthy Me Relationships Changing Me
Relationships and Sex Education is taught in an age-appropriate and sensitive way as part of our wider PSHCE curriculum. Before the teaching of the Changing Me unit each year, parents and carers are informed about the content that will be covered and are given the opportunity to view the materials and ask any questions. We value working in partnership with families and encourage open communication to support children's learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
Science stimulates and excites children’s natural curiosity about phenomena and events in the world around them, as well as satisfying their curiosity for knowledge.
Through scientific activities, we aim to encourage children to be curious about what is happening around them and to develop a positive and practical approach to scientific learning. We also hope to instil a sense of enjoyment. Our children are encouraged to question and discuss science-based issues that may affect their own lives and the future of the world.
Pupils also have the opportunity to develop their practical scientific methods, processes and skills through a range of scientific enquire, to answer questions they have generated. They are taught how to recognise and control variables where necessary and can use a range of scientific equipment with accuracy and precision to help them to gather data and results.
Many of our investigations start by the children making a rational prediction and considering things, such as how we will ensure fair or reliable testing throughout. Finally the children will present their findings in a conclusion whether this is in an oral or written form allowing them to evaluate their findings further.
Through work on experimental and investigative science the children are encouraged to be observant, inquisitive and to develop skills of scientific enquiry and experimentation. We enjoy ‘Science Week’ when the whole school gets involved in a range of activities with the support of outside volunteers and parents.

pageCache.text:
Art & Design
At Thorncombe St Mary's, we aim to develop children’s creativity. They have opportunities to draw, paint, print, make collages, use fabrics and threads and use clay. They are taught the skills and techniques, including digital media, and are then given the opportunity to practise them to produce individual and group pieces of work. As children go up through the school, they are encouraged to think critically and develop an understanding about art and design. Every two years the school organises an ‘Arts Week’ which culminates in a parade through the village. We engage local artists, volunteers and parents to support us.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - Computing
pageCache.text:
Computing
Computing
At Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy, we provide an ambitious and progressive computing curriculum that equips children with the knowledge and skills they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world.
Children develop their understanding of computer science, information technology and digital literacy through carefully planned lessons from the Early Years to Year 6. They learn how digital systems work, create and debug simple programs, use technology creatively to communicate and present information, and understand how to stay safe and responsible online.
Our Chromebooks are used regularly across the curriculum, enabling children to apply their computing skills in meaningful contexts and enhance learning in a wide range of subjects. When using digital technology, children benefit from age-appropriate filtering and monitoring systems, alongside regular teaching about online safety, ensuring they can explore the digital world in a safe, secure and responsible way.
By the time they leave Thorncombe St Mary's, children are confident, responsible and discerning users of technology, ready for the next stage of their education and life in a digital world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - English
pageCache.text:
English
At Thorncombe St Mary's, we strive to develop confident, articulate communicators who enjoy reading, writing and sharing their ideas. Through high-quality texts and engaging learning experiences, we inspire children to become enthusiastic readers and purposeful writers.
Reading lies at the heart of our curriculum. We foster a love of reading through carefully chosen class texts, inviting reading environments and adults who model a passion for books. In Reception and Key Stage 1, children learn to read through the Read Write Inc. phonics programme, while regular assessment allows us to quickly identify and support children who need additional help.
Writing opportunities are planned across the curriculum, giving children meaningful reasons to write for a range of audiences and purposes. Alongside writing, children develop strong speaking, listening and vocabulary skills through discussion, drama, presentations and collaborative learning. Grammar, punctuation and spelling are taught both within English lessons and through discrete sessions to help children apply these skills confidently in their writing.
One of the ways we celebrate children's progress is through our 'Writing Through the Years' books. These special books travel with each child from Reception to Year 6, creating a wonderful record of their writing journey. Children, families and staff can look back and see how their skills have developed over time - from early mark making and letter formation to writing sentences, paragraphs and increasingly sophisticated pieces using a wide range of grammar, punctuation and vocabulary.
From the Early Years onwards, children develop their handwriting through a progressive approach, beginning with mark making and letter formation before moving on to joined handwriting. Throughout their time at Thorncombe St Mary's, children revisit key learning, receive timely feedback to address misconceptions, and are encouraged to take pride in producing high-quality work.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - Geography
pageCache.text:
Geography
At Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy, we aim to inspire children's curiosity and fascination about the world around them. As a small rural village school, we believe it is important that our children develop both a strong understanding of their local area and an appreciation of the wider world.
Through an ambitious and progressive curriculum, children develop their knowledge of locational and place knowledge, human and physical geography, and geographical skills and fieldwork. They learn to ask questions, interpret maps, collect and analyse data, and understand how people and environments interact.
Geography learning is carefully sequenced so that children regularly revisit and build upon their previous knowledge, helping them to remember key concepts and make connections between different places and topics over time. We encourage children to compare locations, identify similarities and differences, and consider how physical and human processes shape the world around us.
Wherever possible, learning is enriched through fieldwork and first-hand experiences. Children explore our local area, developing practical geographical skills while investigating the features of Thorncombe and the surrounding countryside. They also study contrasting locations across the UK and the wider world, helping them to become informed, responsible global citizens who understand the importance of caring for our environment and the communities within it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - History
pageCache.text:
History
At Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy, we aim to inspire children's curiosity about the past and develop a lifelong interest in history. Through an ambitious and engaging curriculum, children explore the history of Britain and the wider world, developing an understanding of how the past has shaped the present.
As they progress through the school, children build their knowledge of significant people, events and civilisations while developing key historical skills such as chronology, historical enquiry, interpreting evidence and comparing different periods in time.
History learning is carefully planned so that children regularly revisit and build upon their previous knowledge, helping them to remember key learning over time and make meaningful connections between different periods in history. We encourage children to consider how historical events and significant individuals have influenced the world we live in today.
Wherever possible, learning is brought to life through high-quality texts, educational visits and our local area. For example, children visit Lyme Regis to explore the life and discoveries of Mary Anning and investigate Thorncombe and the surrounding area to identify how places have changed over time. These first-hand experiences help children to make meaningful links between the past and present, bringing history to life and deepening their understanding.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - Mathematics
pageCache.text:
Mathematics
Mathematics is an essential life skill, providing the foundations for everyday life, financial understanding, science, technology and engineering. At Thorncombe St Mary's, we aim to develop confident, resilient mathematicians who enjoy exploring patterns, solving problems and explaining their thinking.
We teach mathematics every day using the White Rose Maths approach, ensuring that children build fluency, develop reasoning skills and become confident problem solvers. New learning is carefully built upon prior knowledge, with regular opportunities to revisit key concepts, identify and address misconceptions alongside adults, and deepen understanding over time.
Children use a range of practical resources and pictorial representations to support their learning before moving on to abstract methods. We follow a clear calculation policy to teach the four operations, alongside a structured fluency curriculum that develops number facts, times tables and mental maths skills from Reception to Year 6. Wherever possible, children apply their mathematical knowledge across the wider curriculum and in meaningful real-life contexts, helping them to understand the importance and relevance of mathematics beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - RE
pageCache.text:
RE
At Thorncombe St. Mary’s, we use a creative approach to teach RE, incorporating art, music and drama into our study. Pupils learn about Christianity and also about other principal world religions such as Judaism, Hinduism and Sikhism. RE, however is not only about understanding specific religious traditions. It offers pupils the opportunity to think about their own lives, values, attitudes or beliefs and the chance to express their thoughts and ideas in a variety of ways.
The study of Christianity is at the heart of our curriculum. We follow the Christian calendar and embed the core Christian values throughout our teachings of other faiths. Being a county-border school, we use the Devon & Torbay syllabus in conjunction with the Understanding Christianity scheme which provides a systematic and consistent process which enables children to develop their understanding of religious traditions of our increasingly diverse society. The principal aim of 'Understanding Christianity' is to engage pupils in enquiring into big questions arising from the study of religion, belief, philosophy and ethics. In doing so Religious Education will support pupils’ own personal moral, philosophical, ethical and spiritual development and promote respect for others.
As a Church of England school, we take seriously our role of presenting Christianity as a living faith. A close link with the church community is encouraged so pupils can see Christian Life, Worship and commitments at every opportunity. We also make a point of marking the celebrations of the Christian Year to deepen understanding and support our Christian ethos.

Design & Technology
‘DT’ incorporates many traditional skills – cooking, model making, drawing and sketching, problem solving, observation and discussion – putting them together in an approach which encourages the children to become designers and inventors. The children are taught how to use tools and materials safely and economically. As children move through the school, they learn about design, how to make something, how to evaluate their design and others and to apply their technical knowledge and understanding. Children are also invited to use the facilities at local secondary schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Thorncombe, St Mary's CE Primary Academy - Early Years Foundation Stage
pageCache.text:
Early Years Foundation Stage
Our Early Years Foundation Stage welcomes children from Little Acorns Nursery through to Reception, providing a nurturing, stimulating and ambitious start to their education. We recognise that every child is unique and create an environment where children feel safe, valued and inspired to explore, play and learn.
Our curriculum is carefully planned around the seven areas of learning, while also responding to children's interests and individual next steps. Through a balance of child-initiated play, adult-led learning and first-hand experiences, children develop the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for future learning. We place a strong emphasis on communication and language, early reading and writing, mathematics, physical development and personal, social and emotional development, alongside opportunities to explore the world through expressive arts, creativity and outdoor learning.
Children benefit from strong relationships with experienced Early Years staff who know them well. Ongoing observation and assessment enable us to identify children's next steps quickly and provide the right level of challenge and support. Learning is carefully sequenced, with children regularly revisiting and building upon previous experiences to deepen their understanding and confidence.
In Reception, children learn to read through the Read Write Inc. phonics programme, giving them a strong foundation for reading and writing. Throughout the year, staff use ongoing assessment alongside the statutory Reception Baseline Assessment and the Early Years Foundation Stage Profile to monitor progress and celebrate each child's achievements.
We value the important partnership between home and school. We use Tapestry to share children's learning with families, celebrate their achievements and communicate next steps. Parents and carers are encouraged to contribute their own observations from home, helping us to build a complete picture of each child's learning journey and ensuring we work together to support every child to thrive.

Phonics
RWI at Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy
At Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy we aim for all our children to become fluent, confident readers who are passionate about reading.
Children who read regularly or are read to regularly have the opportunity to open the doors to so many different worlds!
More importantly, reading will give your child the tools to become independent life-long learners.
We can achieve this together through:
At Thorncombe St Mary's, we use Read Write Inc Phonics (RWI) to give your child the best possible start with their Literacy development.
What is Read Write Inc?
Read Write Inc (RWI) is a phonics complete literacy programme which helps all children learn to read fluently and at speed so they can focus on developing their skills in comprehension, vocabulary and spelling. The programme is designed for children aged 4-7.
RWI was developed by Ruth Miskin and more information on this can be found at https://youtu.be/sjlPILhk7bQ
How will RWI be taught?
All children are assessed half termly by our RWI lead teacher. From these assessments children are grouped into stages, where they work with peers on the same stage in small groups, each led by a RWI Trained member of staff.
In Nursery, when children are ready, children will be introduced to the single sounds in short five minutes sessions.
In Reception all children will learn how to ‘read’ the sounds in words and how those sounds can be written down.
Progressing through the stages
Children follow the same format as Early Years but will work on complex sounds and read books appropriate to their reading level. Daily sessions of RWI phonics last 45 minutes. Once children become fluent speedy readers they will move on to the RWI Spelling programme, which entails a 15 minutes daily session.
Children will be taught how to read as follows:
Before you start to teach your child the sounds, we focus on naming the pictures for each single sound. For example, mountain, apple and snake. We then introduce the sound. For example, ‘m’, ‘a’ and ‘s’. These are the sounds we use to speak in English. Children initially begin using pictures and letter formation phrases for each sound; this will help children recognise the sound and then form the shape of the sound. For example, ‘m’, ‘mmmmountain’, ‘Maisie Mountain Mountain’.
We use pure sounds (‘m’ not’ muh’,’s’ not ‘suh’, etc.) so that your child will be able to blend the sounds into words more easily. Use the link below to support your pronunciation of the sounds correctly.
https://youtu.be/TkXcabDUg7Q
At school we use a puppet called Fred who is an expert on sounding out words! We call it, ‘Fred Talk’. E.g. m-o-p, c-a-t, m-a-n, sh-o-p, b-l-a-ck.
The following video is an example of blending sounds with Fred: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dEzfpod5w_Q
The children are taught the sounds in 3 sets.
Set 1 sounds are taught in the following order, together with rhymes to help children form the letters correctly and instantly recognise sounds ready for blending.
The children are then taught Set 2 Sounds - the long vowels. When they are very confident with all of set 1 and 2 they are taught Set 3 Sounds.
Nonsense words (Alien words)- What 'a load' of nonsense!
As well as learning to read and blend real words children will have plenty of opportunities to apply their sound recognition skills on reading ‘Nonsense words’. These words will also feature heavily in the Year One Phonics Screening check in the summer term.
RWI Parent Video: The Phonics Screening Check: https://youtu.be/LbKGLJPp6ww
Within all the RWI Speed Sound sessions and Core Storybook sessions, children will be exposed to red and green words to learn, to help them to become speedy readers. Red words are words that are not easily decodable. Story green words are the main words within a specific text and are linked to the sounds that they have been learning. They aim to extend children’s vocabulary. On day one of introducing a new Core Story book, we make sure that children can read each of these Story Green words and ensure that they know what each of these words mean. Speedy Green words are also specific to a particular text, and these words are read using Fred in your Head. The aim is for children to read these words with fluency, at 1 word per second.
​​​​​​​Dots and dashes represent the sound each letter makes. We teach children to read each of these words in a specific way; firstly they look for any Special Friends, e.g. sh, ch or oo, then they Fred Talk, (orally blend), and then they read the word. Eventually they will learn to read words using only ‘Fred in their Head’, (secret Fred Talk)!
The Read Write Inc. One-to-one Phonics Tutoring offers individual tuition to children who are at risk of falling behind with their reading, or are behind their peers, or are new to a school and need to catch up. RWI has the approach, ‘Keep up not Catch up’. This extra 1:1 tutoring will ensure that these children are caught before they fall behind and that every child will learn to read. These sessions are called ‘speed minutes’ and ‘pinny time’.
Listening to your child read at home:
Every third day, your child will bring home a Core Story Book that they have been focusing on in school over 3 days. This book will be closely matched to the sounds and words they know, so they should be able to read all the words with accuracy after the 1st read. They then re-read this book in school, to develop their fluency and by the 3rd read, you are encouraging your child to read this book with a story teller’s voice.
This is a time for children to read with confidence and to experience success as a reader!
On the 3rd day, your child will also bring home an additional book. This will either be a book bag book, linked closely to the core story book that they are reading, a non-fiction book, or a core story book that they have previously read.
Each week, your child will also bring home a school library book, chosen by them, to share with you at home. This is to help encourage their love of reading.
RWI Parent Video: Why Read to your Child? - https://youtu.be/kjHqJQ8sxs4
A large selection of RWI books can also be accessed on https://www.oxfordowl.co.uk . Each child will have their own unique log in to have access.
Useful websites for Parents

SEND
We promote high achievement for all and encourage all children to achieve their full potential. We are an inclusive school and promote equality for all.
We are proud of the relationships we develop with each individual child that enable us to identify any needs as soon as they arise, and to address them. We offer extra support for children with special educational needs and disabilities, and enrichment and challenge for those children who are more able, gifted and talented.
Different levels of support can be provided depending on the needs of the child. Most children will normally be catered within 'quality first teaching' through the differentiation of class work provided by the teacher. However, some children may have a more specific difficulty that may be addressed through a specific intervention programme carried out for a specific purpose for a short period of time.
If the learning difficulty is more general, then the class teacher will plan a programme of extra work for the child that may involve extra adult support. This will be discussed with parents and reviewed regularly through an Individual Education Plan. If we feel unable to provide adequately for the specific needs of the child, then we may involve other agencies for specific support eg speech therapy, educational psychology, behaviour support. We work closely with other schools within our Trust to support this work.
If parents have any concerns, questions or information about their child, then it is vital this information is shared with school staff. We aim to work in close partnership with parents to ensure we meet the needs of all children. In the first instance, parents should contact the child's class teacher, before contacting the SENCO.
More details about our provision for children with special educational needs and disabilities, as well as children with special medical needs, including our approach, policies, what Dorset offers and other useful information is available on the First Federation website at:
SEND and Medical Needs | First Federation
Thorncombe St Mary's CE Primary Academy - SEND
Under the Children and Families Act (2014), Local Authorities are required to publish, and keep under review, information about the services and support available for children and young people who have Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND). The local offer covers provision for children and young people with SEND from birth to 25 and includes information on education, health and social care services and how to access them.
For information on local services and support within Dorset please click here:
As part of this local offer, schools must publish a SEND information report that includes information for identifying, assessing and making provision for pupils with SEND. This needs to be published on the school’s website, kept up-to-date with changes and revised at least annually. The requirements are set out in the SEN Code of Practice.
